net-print/cups: fixup CUPS to run within ChromeOS constraints There are a few constraints for ChromeOS that CUPS doesn't currently satisfy: * we need a read-only rootfs (including /etc/), but CUPS puts some read/write files in /etc/cups/. Particularly, /etc/cups/printers.conf and /etc/cups/ppd/* are generated when printers are added. * we want to run cupsd as an unprivileged user (user name: 'cups'), and CUPS expects specific file ownership/permissions of the configuration files for the user running cupsd So we make the following changes: * drop all use of the lp user/group (we run everything as the cups user instead of separating the "priveleged" and "unprivileged" users) * assign the --with-cups-{user,group}= to 'nobody', as these will essentially go unused by CUPS * have the ebuild create the cups user/group * fix the permissions on the backends in /usr/libexec/cups/backend/. See the linked CUPS mailing-list discussion for details, but essentially, these were marked as "executable only by root" to make sure that CUPS had full permissions to talk to Kerberos and to open up low-numbered ports. Allowing others (e.g., the 'cups' user) will allow IPP to work, albeit without Kerberos support * the upstart job will copy /etc/cups/ into the chronos home directory, then bind mount it over /etc/cups, so we can have a read/write copy. [Note: This was chosen because there doesn't seem to be a clear, consistently-supported way to place the persistent read-only conf files in one read-only directory (e.g., /etc/cups) while putting the read/write conf files (e.g., printers.conf) in another (e.g., /home/...). While it seems this should be possible by setting ServerRoot, this still seems to produce inconsistent behavior.] * disable the CUPS web admin interface (i.e., http://localhost:631) in cupsd.conf; we don't need it, as we're going to create our own UI for it. This doesn't remove the files for supporting it, and it can still be enabled (non-persistently) by running 'cupsctl WebInterface=yes'. Note that I've only changed a few lines in cupsd.conf and cups-files.conf, relative to those provided by the default CUPS build: * uncomment 'ServerRoot' (/etc/cups) * WebInterface (Yes => No) * AccessLog (/var/log/cups/access_log => syslog) * ErrorLog (/var/log/cups/error_log => syslog) * PageLog (/var/log/cups/page_log => syslog) * remove 'Listen localhost:631'; we can just use /run/cups/cups.sock BUG=chrome-os-partner:47758,chrome-os-partner:49267 TEST=build/deploy test image with USE=cups CQ-DEPEND=CL:328020 Change-Id: Ia5a7102bc3dcff3279f2ceffdf93ac43766697c5 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/328011 Reviewed-by: Andrew de los Reyes <adlr@chromium.org>

power: Temporarily disable EcWakeupHelper CL:329948 added a new feature to powerd that needs to call into ectool to control the EC keyboard wake angle. Unfortunately, I only just now Discovered that ectool is only available in test images, and that deploying it on production images is not desired. This patch temporarily disables the EcWakeupHelper that was introduced by that patch until we can implement the appropriate kernel interface to make this work again. It's supposed to be a short-term band-aid to avoid spamming crash reports and intentionally not removing any code yet, since it's not completely clear how the new interface will look and which parts we'll still need yet.
